summary: Jan P. Hogendijk works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Utrecht University (~1974–1983) and held posts at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1983–1985), Utrecht University (~1985), Brown University (~1985–1986), and Leiden University (~2004–2009).

Jan Peter F. Hintelmann specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under doctoral supervisor Marianne Pieper and studied under traditional teachers Thupten Nyandak, Tenzin Kunga, Sonam Senge, and Geshe Sonam Rinchen.

Jan Westerhoff works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Cambridge (~1995–2002) and SOAS University of London (~2002–2004). His posts include Durham University (attested 2011–2013) and the University of Oxford (~2012).

Jan Willem de Jong was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at Leiden University (~1939–1949, PhD) and under Walter Eugene Clark and Paul Demiéville. He held posts at Leiden University (1956–1965) and the Australian National University (1965).

Jan-Ulrich Sobisch is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under David P. Jackson, David Seyfort Ruegg, and Nubpa Rinpoche. His posts include the University of Hamburg, LMU Munich, and the University of Copenhagen (2003–2006).
Jane Bunnag is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of London by 1969, studying under supervisors E. Michael Mendelson and Barbara E. Ward.

Janet Gyatso is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at UC Berkeley (~1974–1981) and held faculty posts at Amherst College (~1988–2002) and Harvard University (~2002).

Janet R. Goodwin works in Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at UC Berkeley under doctoral supervisor Delmer M. Brown and teacher Britten Dean. She held posts at the University of Southern California and University of Aizu (attested 1994).
Jang-Kil Chun specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under doctoral supervisor Minoru Kiyota as well as teachers Paul J. Griffiths, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and Frances A. Wilson.

Janice Dean Willis specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. She studied at Cornell University (~1965–1969) and earned her PhD at Columbia University (~1971–1976) under Alex Wayman. She held a professorship at Wesleyan University (~1977–2014).

Jann Ronis is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Virginia under David Germano, studying also under Jeffrey Hopkins and Khenpo Sönam Tenpa, and held a post there (attested 2007).

Jared Rhoton was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his dissertation at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman by 1985, and also studied under teacher Sakya Trizin.

Jarl Charpentier was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Uppsala University (1902–1908) under Karl Ferdinand Johansson, later studying at the University of Bonn (1908–1909) under Hermann Jacobi. He held posts at Uppsala University starting in 1908.

Jason Birch is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Sydney (BA Hons, 2005) and the University of Oxford (DPhil, 2013) under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at Oxford (attested 2011) and SOAS (attested 2020).

Jason Matthew McCombs specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Michigan and earned his PhD at UCLA (by 2014) under Gregory Schopen, where he was also attested as a lecturer in 2014.

Jason Neelis is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Washington (by 2001) under Richard Salomon. His posts include Ruhr University Bochum (2009–2010) and Wilfrid Laurier University (attested 2013–2021).

Jason Protass works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Stanford University (attested 2015–2016) under doctoral supervisor John Kieschnick, and has held posts at Ryukoku University and Academia Sinica.

Jay Holt Valentine specializes in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Delaware (1992), Naropa University, and the University of Virginia, completing his PhD at Virginia under doctoral supervisor Kurtis R. Schaeffer.

Jay Jasanoff is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Harvard University (~1964–1968). He held academic posts at the University of California, Berkeley (~1969–1970), Cornell University (~1978–1998), and Harvard University (~1998–2022).

Jay L. Garfield works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Smith College (~1999), Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1999), University of Massachusetts Amherst (~2001), University of Melbourne (~2007–2013), and National University of Singapore (~2013–2016).
